result:
The profile page now has a **Delete account** section at the bottom, under Running history. I tested it on copies of your data and clicked through it in a real browser. All the test suites pass, your real database's fingerprint stayed the same, and nothing is committed.

**How it works**
- **Warning:** "This permanently deletes your account and all its plans, runs and history. It can't be undone." Below it, a box asks you to type your username, then the Delete account button.
- **Username doesn't match:** you stay on the profile page with "That username doesn't match. Nothing was deleted." Case matters, so `DEL_A` doesn't match `del_a`; extra spaces around the name are ignored.
- **Username matches:** the account, its plans and its runs are all removed in one step, so it can't half-finish. You're logged out and land on the login page with "Your account was deleted."

**What the tests confirmed**
- Every other user's data was unchanged after a deletion. This included deleting one of your copied accounts on the copy.
- Another browser logged in to the deleted account is logged out too.
- A deleted username can sign up again and starts with an empty account.

**One change you didn't ask for:** new accounts now get a random ID instead of the next number. SQLite can reuse a deleted account's number, so a browser still logged in to the old account could have ended up logged in as the new person. Existing accounts keep their IDs, and the IDs don't appear anywhere on screen.

**Things to know**
- **Old database file:** `instance/training.db`, from the earlier version, still holds one old account and 41 runs. The app no longer uses that file, so Delete account can't remove them. You can delete the file yourself if you don't want it kept.
- **Your real data:** the only plan now belongs to `phareth1`, and `phareth` has none. Your login page still prefills `phareth`, so check you're not expecting plans under that name.
- **Test scripts:** several failed at first because they assumed your earlier data or wording, such as the old account layout and how "doesn't" is written in the page's HTML. I corrected those scripts in my temporary test folder, and the app itself didn't need fixing.

Restart the app to see this. The login and signup templates are unchanged, and the README now mentions the option.
